title: Comair 3272
summary: Flight 3272 on approach to Detroit descended to 4,000 feet and was instructed to turn left to intercept the localizer. During the turn, the captain noted the low speed indicator and requested more power from the first officer. The aircraft abruptly stalled with a thin rough accretion of ice on the lifting surfaces. The aircraft rolled violently 145 degrees left, right, and left again as the crew lost control. The stall was attributed to inadequate icing procedures and failure to activate de-icing boots.
probable_cause: Aerodynamic stall and loss of control caused by aircraft encountering a thin rough accretion of ice on the wings while operating at a low airspeed in icing conditions. Contributing factors included inadequate FAA standards for icing operations, inadequate Comair procedures for icing conditions, crew failure to activate de-icing boots contrary to manufacturer recommendations, and operation near the lower end of the flight envelope while flaps were retracted.

factors.evidence: Aircraft accumulated thin rough accretion of ice on lifting surfaces in icing conditions
Crew did not activate deicing boots on wings contrary to manufacturer instructions; Comair procedure was incorrect due to concern over ice bridging from older aircraft no longer valid for EMB-120
Aircraft operating at low airspeed on approach with flaps retracted; captain requested power to increase speed
Crew inadequately trained for icing conditions and stall recovery in this aircraft type
Comair flight manual procedures for icing conditions were inadequate and did not follow manufacturer recommendations
Aircraft abruptly stalled during approach in icing conditions
Aircraft violently rolled 145 degrees left and right; crew lost control and crashed

events.text: Flight 3272 took off from Cincinnati; less than one hour later began approach to Detroit
Instructed aircraft to descend to 4,000 feet and turn right on heading 180 degrees
Instructed aircraft to turn left on heading 090 degrees to intercept localizer
Captain stated looks like your low speed indicator; requested increased power from first officer
Aircraft abruptly stalled; violently rolled 145 degrees left to right and back to left; crew lost control and aircraft crashed into rural field killing all 29 aboard

notes: NTSB determined clear probable cause related to icing procedures
similar accident (American Eagle 4184) noted with same causal pattern
